source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Water treatment protocols being considered relevant mainly to peritoneal dialysis specifically, rather than to hemodialysis treatment as well at the same facility","B":"Water quality monitoring being treated as an entirely optional step that is left up to each individual dialysis facility's own internal preference","C":"Water quality carrying fairly little established relevance to the overall safety of the entire hemodialysis treatment process performed at the facility","D":"Water used in the dialysis process comes into contact with the client's blood (via the dialysate), so contamination could introduce pathogens or toxins directly into the bloodstream"}}
source_row.rationale: Strict water treatment and quality monitoring is critical in dialysis facilities because water used in the dialysis process comes into contact with the client's blood (via the dialysate across the dialyzer membrane), so contamination could introduce pathogens or toxins directly into the bloodstream, a unique and serious safety consideration in hemodialysis.
